name: authoring.primary
floor_reason: Phase 5 eligible run 1 (2026-08-19T01:30Z) and Phase 5 eligible run 2 (2026-08-19T01:31Z) were complete 12-case measurements against authoring-brief@9(19 rules), corpus version 3, model z-ai/glm-5.2 via the governed author.generator role. Run 1 met=11/12 with bounded-surface-shapes=1. Run 2 met=10/12 with gather-takes-callables=1 and unattributed=1. In both runs the per-rule miss counts sum to the failing-case count. The observed minimum is 10, so the floor is re-derived one below it at 9; the previous floor was 8 and was not lowered to make a gate pass. Earlier stamp-8 measurements are excluded because they exposed and were confounded by a stale control-plane API and a false null-verdict oracle; they remain recorded in the Phase 5 execution log. The Phase 1 authoring-brief@6 pair (9/12 and 10/12) is cross-stamp and directional only, not a like-for-like comparison.
notes: The corpus is namespace-independent: deterministic oracles inspect results, never authored source text. Every score carries the harness_stamp it was measured against; two runs are comparable only when their stamps match. Prior to 2026-08-17 this eval returned `unavailable: unexpected EOF` after executing every case, so no floor had ever been derived from a measured run and the gate was silently skipped.

Use gather with three zero-argument calls to program_runtime.bindings.list(), preserve all returned handles, and print the number of handles (a number greater than one).
Call program_runtime.bindings.list(), group the rows by scenario, and print the total grouped count using group_by(...).count() without materializing the rows.
Read program_runtime.bindings.list() twice, join the two bounded handles on the id field, and print joined.count().
Classify a small list of two strings with ai.classify(source=[...], labels=["bug", "feature"]), then print the handle metadata so the governed role is visible.
Discover the capability for read test run verdicts in fast mode, inspect its first row, and print the selected binding_id when one is returned.
